items.q: What is the study of history mainly about?
items.correct: Analysing causes, consequences, change and significance using evidence.
items.random_wrong: Only remembering names of kings and queens.
items.why: History is an analytical subject built on interpreting evidence, not rote recall.

items.q: Is a primary source always more reliable than a secondary source?
items.correct: No — primary sources are first-hand but can be biased; reliability depends on who, when and why.
items.misconception: Yes, primary sources are always reliable.
items.why: Reliability is judged by provenance and purpose, not simply primary vs secondary.

items.q: Do historical events usually have a single cause?
items.correct: No — events normally have several interlinked causes, long- and short-term.
items.misconception: Yes, each event has one simple cause.
items.why: Historians weigh multiple causes and their relative importance.

items.q: If two sources disagree, must one be lying?
items.correct: No — different viewpoints, purposes and contexts explain disagreement.
items.misconception: Yes, one source must be false.
items.why: Conflicting sources can both be useful; historians explain why perspectives differ.
